subject: Civil Engineering
title: Earned Value Management
description: A micro-lesson that makes Earned Value Management usable.

hook.text: You've spent 60% of the budget but completed only 40% of the work. How bad is it, exactly?

buildup.text: Earned value management (EVM) compares planned work, completed work, and actual cost.

discovery.text: Schedule variance (SV) shows if you're ahead or behind. Cost variance (CV) shows over or under budget.

twist.text: EVM can forecast the final cost — early warning of overruns months before they become crises.

climax.text: NASA requires EVM on all major programs — it predicted the James Webb Telescope's cost overrun early.

punchline.text: Three numbers — planned, earned, actual — tell you everything about project health.

quiz.question: What does a negative cost variance (CV) in EVM indicate?
options: The project is ahead of schedule
The project has spent more money than the value of work completed — it's over budget
The project is using fewer workers than planned

details.summary: Earned value management integrates scope, schedule, and cost data into a single framework to measure project performance. By comparing the budgeted cost of work performed against actual cost and planned progress, EVM reveals whether a project is ahead or behind schedule and over or under budget.
details.whyItMatters: EVM provides early warning of cost overruns and schedule delays by measuring actual performance against the plan. Without it, problems may not surface until they are too late to correct.
takeaways: Planned Value is the budgeted cost of work scheduled to date
Earned Value is the budgeted cost of work actually completed to date
Cost Variance and Schedule Variance reveal performance deviations

faq.question: How does earned value management detect schedule delays?
faq.answer: Schedule Variance equals Earned Value minus Planned Value. If less work has been completed than planned (EV is less than PV), the schedule variance is negative, indicating the project is behind schedule. The Schedule Performance Index (EV divided by PV) shows the rate of schedule achievement.

faq.question: What are the limitations of earned value management in construction?
faq.answer: EVM requires accurate progress measurement, which is subjective for partially complete activities. It tracks the original plan baseline and may not reflect re-planned schedules. Physical completion percentage is often estimated rather than measured precisely.
